newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends firmer, off highs as Dow dips.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends firmer, off highs as Dow dips.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 share index edged closer to its record peak, lifted by a buoyant bank sector.
The leading blue chip index finished 19.8 points higher at 4,681.6, just 12.3 points off its all-time closing high set on May 16.
But trading volume was light, with many dealings rooms thinned out on the back of the long holiday weekend. By 1535 GMT, SEAQ volume registered only 536.4 million shares.
Also, gains were not broad based. FTSE 100 decliners narrowly outpacing advancers 50 to 44.
Bank shares continued to outperform the broad market as institutions, still flush with cash, scrambled to increase their weightings ahead of the Halifax Building Society flotation on June 2.
"We're seeing an unprecedented squeeze," said one trader of the sector's recent performance. "It's being driven by these upcoming flotations."
Shares in Barclays Plc added 33p to 1271-1/2, while HSBC Holdings Plc jumped 40-1/2p to 1884-1/2. Shares in Abbey National Plc rose 11p to 943-1/2.
Lloyds TSB Group shares rose 18-1/2p to 636-1/2, having set a record at 640p earlier. They were among the most actively traded in London.
"I can't help feeling the bubble will burst soon, but it probably will happen after the flotations rather than before," said another trader.
Non-financial stocks generally fared worse, as rising bond yields wore on investors' nerves, traders said.

"The (U.S.) bond market is getting to a level where we could see a major shake-out. With the yield touching the magic seven percent level, a pull-back on Wall Street has to be seen as more than just a distant possibility," said another.
Equities traditionally become less attractive to investors when bond yields rise.
A weaker U.S. bond market knocked the Wall Street lower after its record run last week. The Dow was down 21 points when London markets close.
Panmure Gordon economist Stuart Weatherby said he didn't believe a correction in U.S. stocks would derail the rally in UK blue chips.
"People are talking about a correction (on Wall Street), but I don't think it will be a major detriment to UK equities," he said.
Institutions cannot afford to hold cash and foreign investors have also lined up, scooping up the most liquid UK shares, he said.
"The UK market is well supported by this liquidity situation," said Weatherby, whose year end target for the FTSE 100 was 5,000.

Among the biggest losers on the FTSE 100 were shares in EMI Plc, which lost almost four percent, or 43-1/2p, closing at 1177-1/2. The shares were depressed by a restructuring charge and the impact of sterling's strength on the company's full-year results, dealers said.
Rolls Royce Plc shares fell 8p to 242-1/2 on worries over the company's Trent 700 aircraft engine, dealers said.
Two Hong Kong airlines - Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Dragonair - on Saturday ground their fleet of aircraft powered by the Trent 700.
Shares in British Airways Plc eased 14p to 711-1/2 as investors locked in profits after a recent good run, dealers said.
